rationale: Start with a broad gradient at intermediate temperature to locate the full elution window without risking strongly retained missing compounds. The retention and resolution pattern will guide window trimming and targeted slope or temperature changes.
Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity of the sole unresolved pair. Higher temperature should also preserve or improve the current sub-10-minute last-peak time.

Injection 2 reached the maximum CRF; shorten the gradient one step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keep temperature and endpoints fixed to measure whether the critical early pair retains R ≥ 1.5.

Narrowing the gradient window makes the slope intermediate between injections 2 and 3, aiming to restore the early pair to R ≥ 1.5 while eluting the last peak sooner than injection 2. The new endpoint remains comfortably above the estimated last-peak elution fraction.

Shift both endpoints upward while preserving injection 4’s gradient slope to test whether initial weak-solvent time can be trimmed without losing early-pair resolution. Injection 4 remains a fully resolved, maximum-score fallback.

Retain the lower starting fraction needed by the early pair and test a slightly steeper slope than injection 4. The endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction, aiming for a shorter method with all pairs still resolved.

Test a slightly steeper gradient to approach the early pair’s resolution limit while shortening the programmed gradient. The last peak may enter the final hold, but its estimated elution fraction is close to 0.55, so only a short hold should be needed.

The 60 °C series is near its early-pair resolution limit, with injection 7 retaining maximum CRF. Test the low-temperature endpoint against injections 1 and 2 to check for an alternative selectivity regime before refining further.

Test a faster gradient in the low-temperature selectivity regime, where the early pair separates more strongly. Moving to 30 °C and changing slope may split the late cluster seen at 25 °C while bringing the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test whether shifting the gradient window upward improves selectivity in the low-temperature regime while shortening retention. The narrower window also reduces slope, which may help separate the late cluster seen in injection 9.

Raise temperature one step with injection 10’s gradient unchanged to test whether the late cluster resolves before the early pair loses adequate separation. This isolates temperature selectivity in the faster, low-temperature branch while retaining injection 7 as the fastest fully resolved method so far.

Halve the gradient duration relative to injection 8 to test whether slope changes separate its late cluster at the low-temperature endpoint. The early pair had substantial resolution margin at 25 °C, making this a plausible alternative route to a faster maximum-score method.

Return to the successful high-temperature regime and reduce the slope relative to injection 5 to recover early-pair resolution. This tests whether a higher starting fraction can support another maximum-score method with a narrower solvent window.

Test the fine slope boundary between the fully resolved injection 7 and under-resolved injection 3. This slightly steeper gradient may shorten last-peak retention further, although the early pair is expected to be very close to R = 1.5.

Test a higher starting fraction with a shallower gradient to see whether early-pair resolution can be recovered through slope compensation. The endpoint remains above the observed late-elution window, and injection 7 remains the fastest maximum-score fallback.

Reduce injection 11’s gradient slope by 25% to improve its sole unresolved early pair while preserving the temperature that separated the late cluster. This tests for a fully resolved, lower-temperature alternative with the last peak still expected before 10 minutes.

Reduce the slope from 0.075 to 0.065 organic fraction per minute to bring injection 16’s early pair toward full resolution. The higher endpoint avoids an extended final hold, with the last peak expected before 10 minutes.

Maximum CRF is already achieved; test a shallower high-temperature gradient for greater resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. This offers a potentially more robust alternative to injection 7, whose critical pair is only just above the threshold.

Increase the slope slightly from injection 18 to shorten elution while retaining more resolution margin than injection 7. This should preserve maximum CRF and improve the balance between speed and critical-pair separation.

Shorten the programmed gradient and modestly increase slope relative to injection 19, targeting earlier elution with a useful resolution margin. The endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction, so all peaks should remain within the gradient.

Test a slightly steeper slope than injection 13 using the finer slope increment available with a 12-minute gradient. This should place the early pair near R = 1.5 while modestly shortening last-peak retention relative to injection 13.

Preserve injection 2’s successful slope while trimming its unused high-organic gradient segment. This should retain full resolution and approximately 7.5-minute last-peak retention, providing more separation margin than the fastest method from injection 7.

Trim injection 13’s gradient duration and endpoint while making its slope slightly shallower to preserve early-pair resolution. This targets maximum CRF with earlier initial peaks and a lower final organic fraction than injection 13.

Shorten injection 22’s programmed gradient while preserving its slope and early-pair resolution margin. The last peaks will enter the final hold; test whether they remain fully resolved and elute before 10 minutes at this lower endpoint.

Use the final injection to test a slope between two proven maximum-score methods, targeting full resolution with last-peak retention around 7.9 minutes. Injection 7 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method; the theoretical maximum CRF of 1.000 has already been reached.
